REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL
Ledgerline - practice management software for small accounting firms
Issued by Ledgerline Ltd, Bristol. Reference RFP-2026-014.
Responses to procurement@ledgerline.example by 5pm on 14 November.

1. WHO WE ARE

Ledgerline sells software to accounting practices with between three and forty staff. We have 180 firms on our current product, which is a Rails application a contractor built for us in 2017 and extended every year since. It does the job for a ten-person firm and falls over for a thirty-person one. Support tickets are mostly people asking where a document went, and our own staff answer them by opening the database.

We are replacing it. This document describes what the replacement has to do. It is written by people who run accounting practices, not by engineers, so where we have described a mechanism rather than an outcome, please tell us and propose the outcome instead.

2. THE PROBLEM WE ARE SOLVING

A small practice loses most of its margin in two places: chasing clients for paperwork, and not knowing which jobs are late until a deadline passes. Our firms tell us that a bookkeeper spends six to eight hours a week sending the same three emails to the same four clients. At the January self assessment peak, a partner spends their evenings working out which returns are still missing rather than doing the returns.

The replacement has to take the chasing away from people entirely, and it has to make the state of every job visible on one screen without anyone typing a status into a spreadsheet. Everything else in this document is in service of those two sentences.

3. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

We will judge the project on four numbers, twelve months after go-live:
  - 120 of our 180 existing practices migrated onto the new product.
  - Monthly churn below 2%, against 3.4% today.
  - Time spent chasing documents down by 30%, measured from the time entries our firms already record against the admin job code.
  - Net promoter score of 40 or better among practice owners, against 11 today.

4. WHO USES IT

  Practice Owner - owns the firm, sees every client, signs off write-offs
  Accountant - runs the client work, files returns, approves bookkeeping
  Bookkeeper - does the day to day entry, cannot file or invoice
  Client Contact - external, sees only their own company and its requests
  Support Admin - our staff, can impersonate for support with consent

5. FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS

REQ-001  A practice can sign up, verify its email domain and invite staff by email; an invite expires after seven days.
REQ-002  Staff sign in with email and password or with Google Workspace SSO; the practice owner can make SSO mandatory.
REQ-003  Two-factor authentication is available to every user and can be enforced for the whole practice.
REQ-004  A client company record holds trading name, company number, VAT number, year end, and the services we provide it.
REQ-005  Client records can be imported from a CSV export of our current system, with a preview of what will change before it commits.
REQ-006  Each client has a primary contact and any number of secondary contacts, each with their own portal login.
REQ-007  A job is created from a service template (VAT return, year end accounts, payroll run, self assessment) and carries a due date.
REQ-008  Job templates are editable per practice: stages, default assignee role, and how many days before the statutory deadline the job should start.
REQ-009  The job board shows every open job grouped by due week, filtered by client, assignee, service and status.
REQ-010  Dragging a job between stages updates its status and writes an entry to the job history.
REQ-011  Overdue jobs are highlighted and appear in the owner's Monday morning digest email.
REQ-012  Any user can add a note to a job; notes support mentions that notify the mentioned user.
REQ-013  A job can be put on hold with a reason, which pauses its reminders until it is taken off hold.
REQ-014  Document requests list what the client must send (bank statements, receipts, payroll data) with a due date each.
REQ-015  The client sees outstanding requests when they log in to the portal and can upload straight against a request.
REQ-016  Uploads accept PDF, JPG, PNG, CSV, XLSX up to 50 MB per file, and are virus scanned before they are visible to staff.
REQ-017  A request is chased automatically: a reminder three days before the due date, on the due date, and then weekly.
REQ-018  Chasers stop the moment the document arrives, and the client can never be chased for something already supplied.
REQ-019  Staff can mark a supplied document as rejected with a reason, which reopens the request and tells the client why.
REQ-020  Every document is versioned; an older version can be viewed but never overwritten silently.
REQ-021  Documents can be tagged to a financial year so that the year end pack can be assembled in one click.
REQ-022  The year end pack exports as a single indexed PDF plus a ZIP of the original files.
REQ-023  Staff record time against a job with a start/stop timer or a manual entry, to the nearest six minutes.
REQ-024  Time entries are approved weekly by the practice owner before they can be billed.
REQ-025  A client can be billed on a fixed monthly fee, on time and materials, or on a fixed fee per job.
REQ-026  Invoices are raised in the app, numbered sequentially per practice, and emailed as a PDF with a pay link.
REQ-027  Clients pay by card or direct debit; a failed payment retries twice and then notifies the practice owner.
REQ-028  The practice sees an aged debt list and can send a statement of account to a client in one click.
REQ-029  Recurring monthly fees are generated on the first working day of the month and can be previewed before sending.
REQ-030  A filing is prepared inside the app, checked by an accountant, and only then submitted onward to HMRC.
REQ-031  Any filing submitted is stored with its submission receipt and cannot be edited afterwards.
REQ-032  A deadline calendar shows every statutory date per client for the next twelve months.
REQ-033  Deadlines are derived from the client's year end and VAT scheme, not typed in by hand.
REQ-034  The client portal is white-labelled: the practice's logo, colours and its own subdomain.
REQ-035  Portal users see only their own company; a contact linked to two companies switches between them explicitly.
REQ-036  An e-signature request can be sent for accounts and engagement letters, with a signed copy filed against the client.
REQ-037  Engagement letters are generated from a template with the practice's standard terms and the agreed fee merged in.
REQ-038  The practice dashboard shows jobs due this week, jobs overdue, unbilled time, and cash collected this month.
REQ-039  A report shows write-offs by client and by staff member for the last four quarters.
REQ-040  A report shows recovery rate per job template so the practice can see which services lose money.
REQ-041  Reports export to CSV and to a scheduled email, weekly or monthly.
REQ-042  Notifications are configurable per user: in-app only, in-app plus email, or a daily digest.
REQ-043  The audit log records who did what to which record, with a timestamp and IP address, and is read-only.
REQ-044  The audit log is exportable for a date range by the practice owner and by our support admin.
REQ-045  A practice can export everything it holds (clients, jobs, documents, time, invoices) as a ZIP without asking us.
REQ-046  A practice can request deletion of its data; it is soft deleted for 30 days and then removed for good.
REQ-047  Support staff can only impersonate a user after the practice owner grants consent, and every session is logged.
REQ-048  The app must work on a tablet for staff who visit clients, and the portal must work on a phone for clients.

5.1 FURTHER FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS

REQ-049  A saved view on the job board can be shared with the whole practice or kept private to one user.
REQ-050  Bulk actions on the job board: reassign, change due date, or send the same document request to many clients at once.
REQ-051  A client can nominate an agent (their spouse, their bookkeeper) who sees the same requests without seeing the invoices.
REQ-052  Every email the system sends is visible in the client's record, so staff can see what was already asked.
REQ-053  Inbound email to a per-job address files the attachment against that job automatically.
REQ-054  A search box finds a client by name, company number, VAT number or contact email, in under a second.
REQ-055  Deleted items go to a practice-level bin for 30 days and can be restored by the practice owner.
REQ-056  The system flags a client whose VAT return has been filed late twice in a row, for the owner to review.
REQ-057  Onboarding a new client runs a checklist: engagement letter, identity verification, proof of address, authorisation with HMRC.
REQ-058  Identity verification for a new client contact is done in the portal by photographing a passport or driving licence.
REQ-059  An accountant can copy last year's job set for a client into this year with due dates shifted by one year.
REQ-060  The practice can set its working days and holidays so that no reminder is sent on a day nobody is in.

6. INTEGRATIONS

INT-01  Xero and QuickBooks Online: read the client's trial balance and post journals back, OAuth per client, token refresh handled for us.
INT-02  HMRC Making Tax Digital: VAT obligations, submissions and receipts, through the HMRC developer API with fraud prevention headers.
INT-03  Companies House: pull company number, registered office and year end when a client is created.
INT-04  Stripe: card payments and direct debit for client invoices, plus our own subscription billing.
INT-05  DocuSign or equivalent for e-signature; the vendor may propose an alternative with the same audit strength.
INT-06  Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 for SSO and for calendar entries against job deadlines.
INT-07  An SMS gateway for the final chaser only, because clients ignore email by then.
INT-08  Slack: a channel notification when a filing is submitted or rejected.

7. NON-FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS

NFR-01  Availability of 99.9% measured monthly, excluding a published maintenance window on Sunday between 02:00 and 04:00 UK time.
NFR-02  A page load of under two seconds on a 4G connection for the client portal, measured at the 95th percentile.
NFR-03  A document upload of 50 MB must complete in under 60 seconds on a 10 Mbps connection.
NFR-04  All data is held in the United Kingdom or the European Economic Area; no personal data leaves that boundary.
NFR-05  GDPR: a data processing agreement, a record of processing, and an answer to a subject access request within 30 days.
NFR-06  Cyber Essentials Plus at go-live, with SOC 2 Type II inside 18 months.
NFR-07  Encryption in transit with TLS 1.2 or better and at rest for documents and database backups.
NFR-08  Backups every hour with a 24-hour recovery point objective and a four-hour recovery time objective, tested twice a year.
NFR-09  Penetration test by an independent CREST-accredited firm before go-live and annually after that.
NFR-10  WCAG 2.2 AA for the client portal, which is used by people who are not comfortable with software.
NFR-11  Audit records retained for seven years; client documents retained for seven years after the engagement ends.
NFR-12  A single practice may hold 3,000 client companies and 500,000 documents without the job board slowing down.
NFR-13  Support for 400 practices and 2,500 concurrent users at the January self assessment peak.
NFR-14  No shared database between practices unless row-level isolation is proven in a test we can watch.
NFR-15  Session timeout after 30 minutes of inactivity for staff and 15 minutes for the client portal.
NFR-16  Every outbound email must pass SPF, DKIM and DMARC from the practice's own domain where they configure it.

8. TECHNICAL CONSTRAINTS

Our team is four engineers who write TypeScript. Whatever we buy or build, we have to run it after you leave, so the answer has to be a stack they can hold: TypeScript on the server and in the browser, PostgreSQL for data, and AWS in eu-west-2 for hosting. We are already in AWS, with our documents in S3 and our current database in RDS, and we do not want a second cloud account to reconcile. Infrastructure should be described in code; we use Terraform today.

The existing Rails monolith stays up for the migration and is switched off afterwards. It exposes a read-only REST API we built for the migration, documented in Appendix C. Nothing new should be written into it.

We do not want a mobile app in this phase. The staff view has to work on an iPad in a client's office and the portal has to work on a phone, and that is the whole of our mobile requirement.

9. MIGRATION

180 practices, 41,000 client companies, 2.1 million documents, and eleven years of time entries. We expect a dry run per practice, a report of what did not come across, and a switch that a practice makes itself when it is ready, not a big-bang weekend. Documents keep their original upload dates. Invoice numbering continues from where the old system stopped.

10. COMMERCIALS AND TIMELINE

The budget is 250,000 pounds including VAT for the build, plus up to 40,000 pounds for the first year of hosting and third-party fees. We will not consider a proposal that needs more than that without saying so clearly in the summary.

Dates: contract signed by 1 December. A pilot with five friendly practices, running real client work, fourteen weeks after that. General availability nine months after contract. The January self assessment peak is untouchable: nothing ships between 5 January and 5 February.

12. APPENDIX B - GLOSSARY

MTD - Making Tax Digital, the HMRC programme that requires VAT and income tax to be filed from software.
Year end - The date a company's financial year finishes; it sets most of the statutory deadlines.
Recovery rate - Billed value divided by the value of the time spent, per job.
Write-off - Time that was worked but will not be billed to the client.
Engagement letter - The contract between the practice and the client setting out the services and fees.
Self assessment - The annual personal tax return, due 31 January, which causes our busiest month.
Trial balance - The list of ledger balances pulled from the client's bookkeeping software.
Practice - One accounting firm, which is one tenant in the system.
Portal - The white-labelled area where the practice's own clients log in.
Chaser - An automatic reminder asking a client for a document that has not arrived.

13. APPENDIX C - LEGACY READ-ONLY API

GET /api/v1/practices - list practices with plan and seat count
GET /api/v1/practices/:id/users - staff, role and last login
GET /api/v1/clients?practice_id= - client companies, paginated at 100
GET /api/v1/clients/:id/contacts - contacts with portal flags
GET /api/v1/clients/:id/documents - metadata only, no file bodies
GET /api/v1/documents/:id/download - a signed S3 URL, valid for five minutes
GET /api/v1/jobs?practice_id=&status= - jobs with stage and due date
GET /api/v1/jobs/:id/history - stage changes with actor and timestamp
GET /api/v1/time_entries?from=&to= - time in minutes, approved flag
GET /api/v1/invoices?practice_id= - invoice header, lines and payment status
GET /api/v1/filings?client_id= - type, period and submission receipt reference
GET /api/v1/audit?practice_id=&from= - audit events, capped at 10,000 per call
GET /api/v1/templates - job templates per practice, including stage names
GET /api/v1/deadlines?client_id= - derived statutory dates as the old system calculated them

14. APPENDIX D - QUESTIONS FROM BIDDERS AND OUR ANSWERS

Q1. Can we propose a mobile app anyway?
A1. You can, but it will not win the work on its own and we will not pay for it in this budget.

Q2. Is the 250,000 pound budget firm?
A2. Yes. It is board approved and there is no second tranche.

Q3. Do you need HMRC MTD for income tax as well as VAT?
A3. VAT at go-live. Income tax is in scope for the design, not for the build.

Q4. Who owns the code?
A4. We do, on payment. Third-party libraries stay under their own licences.

Q5. Can the portal use the practice's own domain?
A5. A subdomain of ours is acceptable at launch; their own domain must be possible later.

Q6. How many documents arrive in a peak week?
A6. About 90,000 across all practices in the last week of January.

Q7. What happens to a practice that refuses to migrate?
A7. The old system runs until the end of its contract, then they leave or we move them by hand.

Q8. Do you want us to run the service after launch?
A8. No. Our four engineers run it. Hand over runbooks and be available for 90 days.

Q9. Is offline access needed for the iPad view?
A9. No. It needs to work on a client's guest wifi, which is not the same thing.

Q10. Can you share the current database schema?
A10. Yes, under NDA, once you are on the shortlist.

Q11. Will you accept a phased fixed price?
A11. Yes, phase by phase, with a written scope for each phase before it starts.

Q12. Who signs off the design?
A12. Two practice owners from our advisory group and our head of product, together, in one session.

15. HOW TO RESPOND

Tell us what you would build, what you would not build, and what you think we have got wrong. We would rather read four honest pages than forty polite ones. Include a named technical lead who will be on the project, not on the pitch.
notes: A full RFP, over 20k characters, with the goal stated in section 2 and the metrics in section 3. The test is whether a long document degrades the read: everything is PRESENT and the evidence should come from across the document, not only from its first page.
